name: Frederick G. Williams
role: Scribe and counselor in the First Presidency
dateNote: He became Joseph Smith’s scribe in July 1832 and was ordained a counselor in the presidency on 18 March 1833.
importance: A Kirtland physician baptized in 1830, he was told in section 64 not to sell his farm. He wrote down several revelations, including sections 84 and 87. Section 81, first given to Jesse Gause, later carried his name, and section 90 counts him equal with the presidency. Later revelations direct work on the temple, a home for his family, and the printing office he ran with Oliver Cowdery.
connections: Husband of Rebecca Swain Williams. He served with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon in the presidency and with Hyrum Smith and others on temple and printing work.

sources.title: Frederick Granger Williams, Joseph Smith Papers

reviewNote: Birth, death (10 October 1842, Quincy), baptism, scribe appointment, presidency service (1833–1837), removal (7 November 1837), 1839 excommunication, and 1840 restoration checked on JSP. Scribal roles in 84, 87, and 108 come from the section settings.
